title: Optimize Suggestion Canvas — UX Draft
content:
Purpose and scope

Quick working doc: sketching a unified ‘Suggestion Canvas’ surface in the Redwood Console Optimize tab that surfaces automated recommendations for batching, caching, and quantization. Goal is to make suggestions actionable (one-click apply / preview / schedule), explain expected cost/latency quality tradeoffs, and provide guardrails for safe rollouts.

Audience
- Primary: ML engineers and infra engineers running model-serving workloads on Redwood Dedicated / Private who want cost wins without manual tuning.
- Secondary: Platform/DevOps who will audit/accept recommendations for org policies.

Design principles (compact bullets)
- Action-first: each suggestion should have a clear CTA (preview, apply, schedule).
- Explainable: include an estimate delta with confidence band (tokens/sec, $/1M tokens, p95 latency).
- Safe-by-default: suggestions are proposed as non-disruptive (canary or preview mode) and show fallback behavior.
- Workload-aware: tie suggestions to observed workload slices (short/long sequences, peak windows).
- Audit trail: every apply generates an immutable audit event with before/after metrics.

High-level surface idea
- Top-level banner: single-line summary "X suggested changes for model: gpt-small-8q" with overall expected impact (cost reduction 12–18%, latency change +1–3ms). CTA: "Review suggestions".
- Left column: suggestion list (compact cards). Each card = suggestion type (Batching | Caching | Quantization), severity (low/med/high), tags (cost, latency, quality risk). Cards can be filtered by tag and by workload slice.
- Right column: detail canvas for selected suggestion: explanation, predicted metrics, sample request types impacted, rollout controls, rollback plan, quick links to docs and the infra change diff.

Suggestion card anatomy (fields)
- Title: "Apply batching policy: dynamic batching @ 128ms window"
- Summary line: one-sentence impact and risk e.g., "~15% tokens/sec improvement, <1% quality risk for short-form chat"
- Predicted metrics: cost delta, p50/p95 latency delta, throughput change, expected CPU/GPU utilization change (numbers + confidence interval)
- Workload anchor: example queries / percent of traffic (e.g., 38% of requests have seq_len < 256)
- Buttons: Preview (simulate on replayed trace), Apply (opens rollout modal), Snooze / Dismiss (with reason)
- Contextual links: Jira OPT ticket, Confluence explainer, related model variant

Preview mode details
- Runs a speculative simulation on recent traces (default 24h sample) computing: tokens/sec, cost estimate, and a lightweight quality check (synthetic prompts + eval set).
- UI behavior: preview results show side-by-side current vs projected: small chart and a 3-sentence summary. Preview does not change runtime state.
- Performance caveat: preview may take ~30–90s (async job). Use a progress indicator and keep history of previews.

Rollout modal (Apply flow)
- Target scope: model (single), route (API key), or environment (prod/staging).
- Strategy: Immediate / Canary (percent + duration) / Scheduled (time window)
- Safety gates: max p95 latency delta, model quality regression threshold (measured by pinned eval set), fallback policy (auto-revert on threshold), notification hooks (PagerDuty / Slack)
- Preview of infra diff: what config will change (batch window, kv cache TTL, quantization profile id). Show estimated cost delta and expected GC/eviction behavior.
- Buttons: Confirm & apply | Schedule | Save as suggestion template

Quantization-specific considerations
- Two proposal flavors: offline candidate (requires model artifact swap) vs runtime quantize (dynamic int8 kernels). Distinguish risk and downtime.
- Provide a small table of supported hardware for selected quant profile (A100-v5: supported, T4: degraded accuracy on long sequences).
- Quality checks: include sample outputs from eval prompts, BLEU/ROUGE or embedding similarity score change.

Caching-specific considerations
- Types: prefix KV cache, request-response result cache, adaptive replay cache. Suggest TTL and eviction policy.
- Flagging: suggestions must show cache hit ratio uplift, affected routes and example keys.
- Consistency: indicate whether cache is safe for deterministic ops only or for non-deterministic generation too (replay safety).

Batching-specific considerations
- Tradeoff axis: latency window (ms) vs throughput. Offer presets: conservative (30ms), balanced (80ms), aggressive (200ms).
- For short-form chat use-case show expected token latency percentiles. For long generation show throughput gains.
- Suggest dynamic policy: auto-adjust window based on incoming QPS and latency SLO.

Workload slices and filters
- Ability to pivot suggestions by sample dimensions: sequence length bucket, route, model version, time-of-day.
- Example filter presets: "peak-hour cost-saving" (only consider suggestions that help 6–9pm PST traffic), "low-risk" (max quality risk 0.5%), "multi-tenant safe" (only org-wide policies).

Acceptance criteria for MVP 1 (scope, must-haves)
- Surfacing suggestion cards for batching, caching, quantization based on nightly job analysis (ingest 24h traces)
- Card detail canvas with predicted cost/latency numbers and a concise rationale (short bulleted text)
- Preview simulation that runs on sample traces and returns a summary report (async)
- Apply modal that supports Canary and Immediate strategies with audit records emitted
- Basic filters by model and route; audit trail listing in Optimize activity log

Nice-to-have (post-MVP)
- Automated scheduling recommendations tied to billing cycle or off-peak windows
- ML-based suggestion ranking with confidence calibration and A/B test control
- Team-level permissioning and approval flows (allowlist approvers)
- Explainable quality regression examples: small diff viewer showing before/after tokens for a handful of prompts

Backlog/grooming tickets (draft)
- OPT-4302: suggestion-engine: nightly trace job + suggestion heuristics (initial rules for batching/caching/quant)
- OPT-4303: ui: suggestion list + card component (design tokens, filters)
- OPT-4304: ui: preview simulation endpoint + frontend job status flow
- OPT-4305: ui: apply modal + rollout controls (canary/schedule) + audit event creation
- OPT-4306: infra: safe rollback hook + metrics alert integration (pagerduty/slack)
- OPT-4307: qa: create synthetic eval prompts suite and auto-run harness for previews

Open questions / design tradeoffs (notes for discussion)
- Should previews run on live traces with PII scrub, or only on synthetic/aggregated metrics to avoid data leakage?
- How to quantify quality risk for non-deterministic generation? (embedding similarity vs human eval proxy?)
- Who gets to dismiss a suggestion? Owner only, team leads, or org admins? (audit + ability to re-open)
- How to show uncertainty? numeric CI vs traffic-slice examples?

Microcopy & inline help ideas
- Card tooltip: "Why this suggestion?" -> show the root signal (e.g., "High fraction (42%) of requests had seq_len < 128")
- Preview results header: "Preview (non-destructive) — based on 24h sample"
- Rollout modal CTA: "Apply safely — start a canary for 10% of traffic for 2 hours"

Mini-wireframes (textual)
- [Top] Page header: "Optimize → Suggestions (beta)" [button: Run fresh analysis]
- [Left pane] vertical list: Card 1: "Batching: 80ms window" (cost tag) Card 2: "KV cache: TTL 6h" (latency tag) Card 3: "Quantize: int8 profile-3" (quality-risk tag)
- [Right pane] selected card: big title, small 3-line explainer, 3 KPI boxes (cost, latency, quality risk), chart (current vs projected p50/p95), sample impacted routes list, buttons: Preview | Apply | Snooze
- [Apply modal] top summary line + rollout controls + safety gates + quick confirm

Telemetry & success metrics (what we’ll measure after launch)
- Adoption: % of suggestions viewed, % applied, time from suggestion to apply
- Impact: aggregate cost saved ($/month), average latency change (ms), % of suggestions that triggered rollback
- Trust metrics: false-positive rate (suggestion applied that increased cost or regressed quality)

Implementation notes / edge cases
- For multi-tenant accounts only surface org-scoped suggestions if user has org-admin scope. Otherwise surface route-level non-blocking suggestions.
- Suggestion engine should backfill confidence score. UI should never hide raw numbers behind too much prose — show both.
- Caching suggestions must annotate "stale risk" and provide an opt-out list of endpoints that require no caching.

Next steps (immediate)
- UX sync w/ Marco + Alina: review wireframes + map components to Console design system (this week)
- Eng sync: define minimal payload for preview API + expected runtime trace sample format (OPT-4302)
- PM: prioritize backlog tickets for next sprint and allocate an owner for suggestion engine heuristics

Notes to self (rough todo)
- Get sample traces for 3 customers (chatbot, summarization, search-rerank) to validate heuristics
- Draft preview success/failure UI states and write copy for rollback modal
- Add accessibility checks for the card list (keyboard nav, screen reader labels)

Revision history
